Council approved Bill #250568, authorising the sale of $800 million in bonds to pay for her Housing Opportunities Made Easy (H.O.M.E.) initiative, issued under a service agreement with the Philadelphia Redevelopment Authority. The money subsidises the creation and preservation of 30,000 units built through public-private partnership rather than operated by the city, and her own framing is of streamlining processes and eliminating barriers so that housing gets built. That is subsidy and public financing to get affordable housing built, which is the chair 4 position, rather than chair 3's binding rules on the private market such as rent caps or required affordable units.

Parker signed Executive Order No. 7-25, her One Philly Plan to End Street Homelessness, during her State of the City speech on 19 December 2025. Its Section 1 is operative rather than advisory: it directs the Office of Homeless Services, in coordination with other City agencies, to facilitate access and provide financial support to operate 1,000 new shelter beds, to be operational by 31 January 2026, with on-site wrap-around behavioural health services and work with the Philadelphia Housing Authority on permanent supportive housing supply. Expanding the shelter system by 1,000 beds and directing financial support to operate them is chair 2, expanding services by increasing public funding. It is not chair 3, which is maintaining today's programmes with no major new spending, and it is not chair 1: the order sets a numbered expansion against a deadline rather than a permanent dedicated funding stream or a guarantee of housing.

Parker's first act in office was Executive Order No. 1-24, signed 2 January 2024, declaring a public safety emergency. It is not only a planning document: Section 2.A orders the Police Commissioner to employ any lawful means necessary to abate the emergency and the Department to vigorously enforce existing law, and Section 2.B sets the objective of increasing the number of police officers conducting patrol operations and maximising deployment of the current force. The Department's 100-Day Report, prepared in response to that order, records the delivery: strategies to maximise deployment of current staffing, strategies for increasing the number of officers trained for community policing, and 129 new officers assigned from academy classes to foot beats by the end of June 2024. Adding officers and expanding police presence to deter and respond to crime is chair 4. It is not chair 3, which keeps police as the main responders and adds crisis teams alongside them; the order's named objective is more officers and more patrol.
